rejected.title: What shapes the financial sector
card: Deregulation
the removal or easing of government rules. Fewer rules can let new firms enter and let existing firms offer new products.
New technology
such as online banking and phone apps. It lets customers use financial services at any time without visiting a branch.
Confidence
how positive people and businesses feel about the future. When confidence is high, more people may borrow and spend. When it is low, more may save and borrow less.
These three things can change what the financial sector offers and how people use it.
rejected.remember: Rules, technology and confidence can all change how the financial sector works.

a.q: A government removes many rules that stopped new lenders opening in Australia. Which force is shaping the financial sector?
opts: Deregulation
New technology
Falling confidence
Online banking
a.why: Removing government rules is deregulation, and it can let new lenders enter. Online banking is technology, which is a different force and does not involve changing rules.

b.q: Many Darwin families fear a downturn is coming. Which force is at work, and what is its likely effect on the financial sector?
opts: Low confidence, so demand for loans may fall
Low confidence, so demand for loans may rise
New technology, so demand for loans may fall
Deregulation, so demand for loans may fall
b.why: Fear about the future is low confidence. When confidence is low, more people may save and borrow less, so demand for loans may fall, not rise. The families' feelings are not a change in technology or in government rules.
b.clue: When people worry about the future, do they borrow more or less?
